caption:
Paid for Papa's house? Who owns it? | Inheritance Without a Will Explained

Bought a house in your father's name with your own money? If he passes away without a will, it does not simply come back to you.
Under Hindu succession law, a man's self-acquired property goes first to his Class I heirs: widow, sons, daughters and his mother, one share each.
Illustrative: a ₹60 lakh house, heirs = mother + 2 children, so ₹20 lakh each. Generally, who paid does not decide it; the name on the deed and a will do.

Sources: Hindu Succession Act, 1956, Section 8 and the Schedule (Class I heirs), as explained by a legal-information wiki and a case-law research site. Applies to Hindus, Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists; ancestral property follows different rules; if the father's mother is alive she also takes a share.
